key_claims: Substantial cardiovascular protection (risk reduction >30%) was associated with 560 to 610 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per week.
Meeting the guideline of 150 minutes per week was associated with a modest 8-9% lower cardiovascular risk.
People with lower fitness levels may need about 30-50 additional minutes of exercise per week compared to highly fit individuals to achieve similar benefits.
The study included 17,088 participants from the UK Biobank, with an average age of 57, and recorded 1,233 cardiovascular events over a follow-up of 7.8 years.
limitations: Observational study cannot prove cause and effect.
Cardiorespiratory fitness was estimated rather than measured directly.
Participants may have been healthier and fitter than the general population.
The analysis did not assess sedentary time or lower-intensity exercise.
what_not_to_say: The study proves that higher exercise levels directly cause lower cardiovascular risk.
The study recommends exactly 560-610 minutes of exercise for everyone.
The study shows that 150 minutes of exercise is ineffective.
The study provides personalized exercise targets for individuals.
